## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-general`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-general)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-general`:

$$
2^{O(k\log\log k/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(k(\log\log k)^2/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Compute a factor-2 vertex cover X of the primal graph.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O_q(k)$ |
| Clauses | $L^{O_{q,r}(1)}$ |
| Maximum clause width | $O_{q,r}(1)$ |

## Derivation

1. Each constraint contains at most one variable outside X, since every pair of variables sharing a constraint is adjacent in the primal graph.

2. If an outside variable cannot receive any of its q values, pick one violated incident constraint for each value. The failure depends on at most q(r-1) variables of X.

3. Enumerate and forbid these constant-size boundary assignments, also keeping constraints wholly inside X. Different outside variables can then be extended independently.

4. One-hot encoding of X uses O_q(k) Boolean variables; each forbidden tuple becomes a fixed-width clause. Construction is polynomial-time for fixed q,r, so apply the general-density bound.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- The domain and arity must be fixed, and relations must be given in the stated finite explicit model.
- No counting claim is made because extension multiplicities are discarded.

A decision-preserving kernel does not automatically preserve the number of solutions.
